title: Alibaba Cloud launches sixth data center in Malaysia
html:
Alibaba Cloud has launched its sixth data center location in Malaysia.

As reported by w.media, the company has launched its third data center in its Johor cloud region and its sixth in the country overall.

The Johor cloud region was launched in June 2026, joining an existing region in Kuala Lumpur, which went live in October 2017, at the time making it the first global public cloud platform to host infrastructure in the country.

Speaking during the Qwen Conference Malaysia 2026, Alibaba Cloud's intelligence general manager of Malaysia, Choong Hon Keat, said that the company is seeing increased AI adoption across industries. “Our sixth data center in Malaysia supports this work with more local cloud capacity and reflects our long-term commitment to helping Malaysian organizations of every size benefit from AI.”

This week, Alibaba Group posted its earnings results for Q2 of FY2027. Total revenue for the company was RMB 272 billion ($40.8bn), up 10 percent year on year (YoY), while AI cloud revenue reached RMB 61 billion ($9.15bn), up 53 percent YoY. External cloud revenue similarly grew rapidly, reaching RMB 47 billion ($7.05bn), up 64 percent.

Adjusted EBITDA was RMB 32.6 billion ($4.89bn), a 260 percent increase, which the company attributed to improved operating results in Taobao Instant Commerce and the cloud segment.

Management said during the call that it is expecting its chip unit, T-Head, to start mass production of its next-generation Zhenwy V900 chip in the new year, which it claims offers three times the performance of its M890.

Commenting on this, CEO Eddie Wu said: "As T-Head's capacity ramps up, domestic compute will contribute a higher proportion of our overall compute and will become the primary engine supporting cloud revenue growth, subsequently lowering dependence on overseas compute.

"The market does remain supply-constrained. That is true globally and especially here in China, I think, over the next couple of years, as we continue to advance our full-stack AI products centered on T-Head and supply chain, we see strong visibility towards the previously communicated calendar year 2030 targets of $100 billion in external cloud revenue."

The company has a long-term goal of reaching 20GW of capacity.

This month, a launch event was also held for a 10,000-chip AI cluster in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area powered by Alibaba's Zhenwu AI chips. The data center is owned and operated by China Telecom. It is ultimately planned to scale to 100,000 chips.

The launch of Alibaba's latest data center comes shortly after reports that TikTok owner ByteDance is struggling to get two data center projects in Malaysia off the ground. According to a report from Bloomberg, $488m in financing for data center operator and developer Epoch Digital was delayed, and a site visit did not come to fruition.

Funding of $480m for the purchase of chips for a data center being developed by Aolani Cloud Pte, similarly, has been frozen after the US increased rules for exports of chips to Singapore, Malaysia, and other countries, after the revelation of Nvidia's ex-CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
